card.name: Groups of people before a headcount
card.fires_on: Words right after a group of people is named, where a number or size of the group may come next, such as 'and', 'have', 'children', 'young' or 'nearly'. Seen in history and religious prose about crowds, armies and families.

modes.label: Listing groups of people
modes.description: Linking word or comma after a group such as men, women or children.
modes.example: Men were separated from women<< and>> children, then proceeded for medical exams,

modes.label: Just before a count
modes.description: A word in a sentence about how many people there were, leading into a number.
modes.example: How many men did the Meccans<< have>> fighting?

modes.label: Young or small groups
modes.description: Words like children, young or little describing a group of people or animals.
modes.example: saw a group of<< children>> playing at Christian baptism

card.writes: It lowers the chance of 'thousands' and 'hundreds' style words, so large crowd sizes are less likely next.
card.plain: It marks spots in history text where a group of people is described and a number could follow.
